Iceland's Ring Road circles the entire island, and driving it is one of the most efficient ways to see the country's glaciers, waterfalls, and black-sand beaches in a single trip.

## How long do you need

Most travelers budget seven to ten days for the full loop, though it's entirely possible to drive the road faster if you're comfortable skipping some of the smaller detours.

## What to expect from the roads

Outside the capital region, expect long stretches without fuel stations, so it's worth topping up the tank whenever you pass a town rather than waiting until the gauge gets low.

## Best stops along the way

The south coast alone justifies the trip, with Skógafoss, Seljalandsfoss, and the black sands of Reynisfjara all within a short drive of one another.

Winter driving adds real risk from ice and sudden weather changes, so travelers visiting outside the summer months should check road conditions daily and build slack into the itinerary in case a pass closes unexpectedly.
